description: Congressman Jason Crow (CO-06) seeks a full-time Staff Assistant to serve in his District Office in Aurora, Colorado. Responsibilities include managing the front desk of a fast-paced congressional office, greeting visitors in a professional and courteous manner, answering and logging incoming phone calls, overseeing the district internship program, drafting official correspondence on behalf of the Congressman, and staffing outreach events. Additionally, this position will work closely with the District Director and the Director of Constituent Services to assist with other day-to-day tasks and administrative duties. The annual salary is $50,000 with a competitive benefits package including health insurance, transit benefits/parking, 401(k) retirement match, student loan repayment/tuition assistance, paid family leave, and more.

Successful candidates will have exceptional writing and editing skills, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail. This is not an entry-level position.
responsibilities: Develop and execute a comprehensive communications strategy in partnership with the Chief of Staff that advances the Congresswoman's priorities and reflects the needs and interests of the district.
Serve as the office's primary strategic advisor on communications, messaging, media strategy, and rapid response.
Advise the Congresswoman and senior staff on how to effectively communicate complex legislative and policy issues.
Build and maintain strong relationships with local, regional, and national reporters and media outlets.
Manage day-to-day press operations, including responding to media inquiries, coordinating interviews, pitching stories, and identifying opportunities for coverage.
Draft and edit press releases, statements, talking points, op-eds, speeches, newsletters, media advisories, and other communications materials.
Prepare the Congresswoman for interviews, press conferences, speeches, and other media appearances, including developing briefing materials and conducting media preparation.
Manage a DC-based Press Secretary and oversee the office's digital and social media strategy.

Staff Assistants often provide the first impression of the office to constituents, guests, and other VIPs. The ideal candidate should have excellent attention to detail, a strong work ethic and exceptional written communication skills, an eagerness to learn and grow within the office, and a desire to be part of a highly-collaborative, high-achieving team. The position is full time with a salary of $55,000 and federal benefits, including student loan repayment program (if eligible) and transit or parking benefits.

description: The Island County Community Liaison serves as Rep. Larsen's primary representative to communities on Whidbey and Camano islands. The liaison is responsible for engaging with constituents, businesses, organized labor, nonprofit organizations, federal agencies, tribal governments and federal, state and local officials throughout Island County. The position covers a broad portfolio of federal issues, including military and veterans' affairs, service academy nominations, federal grants, housing, transportation, agriculture, outdoor recreation, access to recreation and outdoor spaces, and other matters assigned by the District Director. The liaison is expected to build strong relationships with community stakeholders, develop a detailed understanding of local projects and policy concerns, and communicate those priorities to the Representative and office staff. The liaison will also help stakeholders understand federal policies, programs, and opportunities that affect Island County. The position is based in Representative Larsen's Everett, Washington office and reports directly to the District Director. District staff work closely with the Washington, D.C., office, and all staff report to the Member and Chief of Staff. This is a full-time position with federal benefits such as health care, the Federal Employees Retirement System, Student Loan Repayment Program, vacation/annual leave, paid sick and parental leave, and others.
responsibilities: Serve as an official representative for Rep. Larsen at meetings, forums and public events
Build and maintain relationships with constituents, businesses, labor, non-profit organizations, federal agencies, tribal and local government, and other stakeholders in Island County
Travel regularly throughout the district to monitor local issues, projects and activities
Work with Washington D.C.-based staff on federal policy development and help interpret federal policies for local stakeholders
Assist constituents and organizations in navigating federal agencies, grants and other federal resources
Plan and coordinate meetings, public events, site visits, and other district activities
qualifications: Strong knowledge of Island County and North West Washington
Experience conducting outreach with government officials, cultural communities, the business community, organized labor and local stakeholder groups
Strong understanding of veteran's issues, active duty and reserve issues, as well as military organizational structures and relevant terminology
Ability to exercise discretion and independent thinking while working as part of a team on sensitive projects and issues
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and comfort with public speaking
Flexibility to work evenings and occasional weekends
A valid driver's license, reliable access to a vehicle and the ability to travel regularly throughout Island County and the congressional district
Self-motivated, great at multi-tasking, with strong interpersonal skills and a teamwork-oriented attitude
Detail oriented and organized
